_note: The Problems lens rules. Detection lives in scan.js; everything the owner will want to tune lives here: whether a rule is on, its threshold, its default severity (bad | warn | ok | info) and its wording. Reloaded on every scan. A project overrides any field in <project>/.cockpit/plugins/architecture.problems.json with the same shape (only the rules and fields it names). The owner's grades set in Cockpit still win over the band here. Each rule may name the doctrine rule it detects (`doctrine`, from prompts/doctrine.md); the legend shows it, so the map is the retroactive check the doctrine asks for. Rules marked slop: true are the AI-slop catalogue - habits of machine-written code; add one when a new model shows a new habit (a count in scan.js slopCounts, a rule here). min = the per-file count that makes a finding. Rules marked slop: true are the AI-slop catalogue - habits of machine-written code; add one when a new model shows a new habit (a count in scan.js slopCounts, a rule here). min = the per-file count that makes a finding. weight = how likely the finding BITES, 1-5 (fake success bites on every failure; a dead route almost never); with churn and tested it makes the likelihood side of the risk matrix. Rules marked shape: true check the four-column shape (Screens -> Actions -> Logic -> Data, arrows one way). Rules marked decl: true check DECLARATIONS (tags.json) against what the code does - the Declarations block on Problems. `stage` names the test stage a rule reports under (plugins/architecture/stages.json). `stage` names the test stage a rule reports under (plugins/architecture/stages.json).

no-single-writer.label: no single writer
no-single-writer.why: a table written from this many files has no owner; a change to its shape has to be found everywhere

sql-in-page.label: SQL in the page
sql-in-page.why: a file that renders HTML and writes the database mixes presentation with data; nothing can be tested or reused on its own

own-db-connection.label: own database connection
own-db-connection.why: more than one file opens its own connection; credentials and settings live in several places

duplicate-function.label: duplicate function
duplicate-function.why: the same function name defined in more than one file - copy-paste twins that drift apart

god-file.label: god file
god-file.why: one file reaching an outsized share of the code and data; everything routes through it

secret-in-code.label: secret in code
secret-in-code.why: a password or key literal in source is in every copy and every backup

nothing-points-here.label: nothing points here
nothing-points-here.why: an entry point, a scheduled script, or dead - the scanner cannot tell which

read-never-written.label: read, never written
read-never-written.why: filled from outside this code - an import, another app, or by hand

defined-never-used.label: defined, never used
defined-never-used.why: a migration creates the table and nothing in this code touches it - either dead schema or owned by something outside this repo

write-never-read.label: written, never read
write-never-read.why: code writes this table and nothing here reads it - a queue with no consumer, or dark data nobody will act on

table-not-in-db.label: table not in the database
table-not-in-db.why: the code names this table and the live database (Database plugin) does not hold it - a rename, a migration not yet run, a test-only table, or prose the scanner took for a table

table-nothing-touches.label: table nothing touches
table-nothing-touches.why: the live database (Database plugin) holds this table and no code here reads, writes or defines it - dead data, or owned by something outside this repo

test-without-assertion.label: test that cannot fail
test-without-assertion.why: a test file with no assertion passes whatever the code does - coverage theater

empty-catch.label: swallowed error
empty-catch.why: an empty catch block: the failure happens and nobody hears - the classic machine-written shortcut

fake-success.label: fake success
fake-success.why: a catch that returns canned data ([] / {} / ok:true / null) with no throw and no log - the caller believes the call worked

todo-stub.label: TODO stubs
todo-stub.why: TODO / FIXME / placeholder / not implemented left in - unfinished work presented as finished

debug-logging.label: debug logging
debug-logging.why: console.log left in a production path (scripts, tests and tooling are exempt)

commented-out-code.label: commented-out code
commented-out-code.why: blocks of code kept in comments "just in case" - git is the just-in-case; the block rots and misleads

unbounded-query.label: unbounded query
unbounded-query.why: SELECT with neither WHERE nor LIMIT - correct on a small table, a stall once it grows

uncapped-retry.label: uncapped retry
uncapped-retry.why: an endless loop that awaits and catches with no attempt cap - a failing dependency becomes a hot loop

type-escape.label: type escapes
type-escape.why: as any / @ts-ignore / : any - the type checker switched off exactly where it complained

dead-route.label: dead route
dead-route.why: an HTTP route nothing in this code calls - an external client, a mobile app, or dead; the scanner cannot tell which

screen-touches-data.label: screen touches data
screen-touches-data.why: a screen reads or writes a table directly - it skipped the action and the logic; nothing checks who asked

sql-in-action.label: SQL in the door
sql-in-action.why: a route file queries tables itself - the door should check who asks and hand off to logic; the query cannot be reused or tested alone

cross-feature-write.label: writes another feature's table
cross-feature-write.why: code in one feature writes a table another feature owns - two owners of one shape; a change to the table breaks a feature that never sees it

line-points-up.label: line points up
line-points-up.why: a shared service depends on a module, or a module on the dashboard - lines point down only, so a lower level can be built, tested and switched on without the one above it (families)

module-reaches-into-module.label: reads another module's tables
module-reaches-into-module.why: a module reads a table another module owns - it should ask that module through its functions; reading its tables couples the two and leaks past its permission checks (families)

undeclared-module-dependency.label: undeclared module dependency
undeclared-module-dependency.why: a module calls or imports another module it does not list under "## Depends on" in its README - an unreviewed line between modules (families)

action-calls-action.label: door calls door
action-calls-action.why: a route file calls another route - the work should be in logic both doors can call

data-reaches-up.label: data reaches up
data-reaches-up.why: a migration or schema file imports code - data defines shape; it never depends on logic or screens

tag-without-readme.label: feature with no README
tag-without-readme.why: a file names a feature that has no README and no mapping entry - a feature exists when its README exists

readme-without-files.label: README with no files
readme-without-files.why: a feature is declared but no file carries its @feature

feature-twice.label: two features
feature-twice.why: a file declaring two features - a file belongs to one

kind-disagrees.label: kind disagrees
kind-disagrees.why: the declared @kind disagrees with what the file does - a logic file declaring routes, a screen reading a table

kind-unknown.label: unknown kind
kind-unknown.why: a @kind value not in the schema

flow-without-test.label: flow without a test
flow-without-test.why: a flow the README defines that no test names - unproven

test-names-unknown-flow.label: test names unknown flow
test-names-unknown-flow.why: a test naming a flow no README or mapping defines

flow-not-in-feature.label: flow of another feature
flow-not-in-feature.why: a screen naming a flow its feature does not define

flow-step-missing.label: flow step names nothing
flow-step-missing.why: a flow step names a screen or action the scan cannot find - a typo, or a step that does not exist yet

purpose-missing.label: no @purpose
purpose-missing.why: a header with no @purpose - one sentence so anyone opening the file knows what it is for

purpose-long.label: @purpose too long
purpose-long.why: more than a sentence; the narrative belongs in the feature README

owned-table-written-elsewhere.label: owned table written elsewhere
owned-table-written-elsewhere.why: a README says a feature owns this table and another feature writes it

listed-table-undefined.label: listed table undefined
listed-table-undefined.why: a README lists a table nothing defines or touches

table-unowned.label: table nobody owns
table-unowned.why: no README or mapping lists this table under a feature (only once any feature is declared)

tag-missing.label: tag missing
tag-missing.why: a file that should carry a tag by the schema's applies-to and does not - the rollout list

tag-unknown.label: unknown tag
tag-unknown.why: a @tag not in tags.json - a tag enters through the schema, never through one file

mapping-redundant.label: mapping entry redundant
mapping-redundant.why: the file's header now carries what the mapping file says - remove the entry; the file empties as the code becomes self-describing

sql-string-built.label: SQL built by concatenation
sql-string-built.why: a SQL string joined to a variable with + - the door to injection; bind parameters instead

eval-use.label: eval
eval-use.why: eval / new Function runs code from data

shell-with-input.label: shell with input
shell-with-input.why: a shell command built from request input - command injection

raw-html-from-data.label: raw HTML from data
raw-html-from-data.why: HTML from a variable rendered without escaping - cross-site scripting

path-from-input.label: path from input
path-from-input.why: a file operation on a path from request input - path traversal

open-redirect.label: open redirect
open-redirect.why: a redirect to a URL from request input

env-committed.label: .env committed
env-committed.why: an environment file in the repository - every clone and every backup has the secrets

secret-in-config.label: secret in config
secret-in-config.why: a password, key or token literal in a config file

secret-in-log.label: secret in a log
secret-in-log.why: a password, key or token written to a log file

env-example-incomplete.label: .env.example incomplete
env-example-incomplete.why: a variable the code reads is not in .env.example - the next machine will not know to set it

migration-edited-after-run.label: migration edited after it ran
migration-edited-after-run.why: a numbered migration changed after the next one existed - copies that already ran it never see the change

lockfile-missing.label: no lockfile
lockfile-missing.why: installs are not reproducible without a committed lockfile

vulnerable-dependency.label: vulnerable dependency
vulnerable-dependency.why: npm audit reports known vulnerabilities in production dependencies

outdated-major.label: outdated major
outdated-major.why: a dependency a major version behind - the upgrade only gets harder

lint-error.label: lint errors
lint-error.why: the project's own linter reports errors in the file

lint-warning.label: lint warnings (5+)
lint-warning.why: five or more lint warnings in the file

test-failing.label: failing test
test-failing.why: a test file failed in the last run - the code is broken or the test is

flow-not-clicked.label: flow not clicked through
flow-not-clicked.why: a flow with a test that calls the pages, but none that clicks them in a browser - a broken button or a dead screen still passes (functional tests are the README flow clicked through)

flow-skipped.label: flow skipped - not proven
flow-skipped.why: its test passed but skipped part of the flow, with a stated reason (a switch off, no storage, a provider login) - grey, not green: what was skipped is unproven

flow-failing.label: flow failing
flow-failing.why: the test that proves this flow failed in the last run

door-open.label: open door
door-open.why: a route answered an unauthenticated request with 2xx in the last run and is not declared public - anyone can call it

contract-break.label: contract break
contract-break.why: a GET route's status or JSON shape changed against what was recorded - screens and external clients depending on it break

migration-irreversible.label: migration cannot come back
migration-irreversible.why: a migration with no .down.sql - the promote script cannot restore the previous release past it

migration-cycle-failed.label: migration cycle failed
migration-cycle-failed.why: up-down-up on the test database failed - a migration or its reverse is wrong

smoke-failed.label: promote smoke failed
smoke-failed.why: the promoted environment did not read back healthy; the script restored the previous release, or could not

sast-xss.label: SAST: Cross-Site-Scripting (XSS) (semgrep)
sast-xss.why: user input reaching a page unescaped - a script anyone can plant runs in every visitor's browser

sast-sql-injection.label: SAST: SQL Injection (semgrep)
sast-sql-injection.why: user input reaching a query as text - the database does what the visitor types

sast-command-injection.label: SAST: Command Injection (semgrep)
sast-command-injection.why: user input reaching a shell command - the machine does what the visitor types

sast-code-injection.label: SAST: Code Injection (semgrep)
sast-code-injection.why: user input evaluated as code (eval and its cousins)

sast-secrets.label: SAST: Hard-coded Secrets (semgrep)
sast-secrets.why: a password, key or token written into the source - anyone with the code has it

sast-crypto.label: SAST: Cryptographic Issues (semgrep)
sast-crypto.why: weak or misused crypto: broken hashes, fixed salts, insecure modes

sast-sensitive-info.label: SAST: Mishandled Sensitive Information (semgrep)
sast-sensitive-info.why: sensitive data logged, echoed or sent where it should not go

sast-authentication.label: SAST: Improper Authentication (semgrep)
sast-authentication.why: a sign-in that can be got around

sast-authorization.label: SAST: Improper Authorization (semgrep)
sast-authorization.why: a door that does not check who is asking

sast-ssrf.label: SAST: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) (semgrep)
sast-ssrf.why: the server fetches a url the visitor chose - reaching inside the network

sast-xml-injection.label: SAST: XML Injection (semgrep)
sast-xml-injection.why: XML parsed with external entities or user input inside it

sast-cookie.label: SAST: Cookie Security (semgrep)
sast-cookie.why: cookies without the flags that keep them off the wire and away from scripts

sast-validation.label: SAST: Improper Validation (semgrep)
sast-validation.why: input trusted without checking its shape

sast-deserialization.label: SAST: Insecure Deserialization (semgrep)
sast-deserialization.why: objects rebuilt from data the visitor controls

sast-path-traversal.label: SAST: Path Traversal (semgrep)
sast-path-traversal.why: a file path built from user input - ../ reaches files it should not

sast-open-redirect.label: SAST: Open Redirect (semgrep)
sast-open-redirect.why: a redirect to wherever the visitor says - phishing through your own domain

sast-csrf.label: SAST: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) (semgrep)
sast-csrf.why: a state-changing request another site can make on the visitor's behalf

sast-other.label: SAST: other (semgrep)
sast-other.why: a semgrep rule outside the classes above: debug code left on, dangerous functions, configuration

sast-failed.label: SAST run did not run
sast-failed.why: semgrep is not unpacked on this engine (Settings > Engine), or it stopped - the report says why

dast-high.label: DAST: high-risk alert
dast-high.why: ZAP found it against the running app - an injection, an exposed secret, an auth bypass; what an attacker finds first

dast-medium.label: DAST: medium-risk alert
dast-medium.why: a weakness ZAP could demonstrate on the running app: missing protections, information leaks, weak headers

dast-low.label: DAST: low-risk alert
dast-low.why: hygiene ZAP noticed from outside - cookie flags, headers, disclosure; cheap to fix, noisy to leave

dast-failed.label: DAST run did not finish
dast-failed.why: the last run stopped before the alerts were read - the report says why

input-crash.label: door crashes on input
input-crash.why: a 5xx on hostile input - the door falls over instead of refusing; every crash is a lever

input-leak.label: door leaks its build
input-leak.why: a stack trace, SQL error or file path in the answer - the app tells an attacker how it is made; answer a plain error, log the detail

input-reflected.label: input reflected unescaped
input-reflected.why: a script tag sent in came back in HTML as-is - cross-site scripting, proven on the running app

input-slow.label: input stalls the door
input-slow.why: one hostile payload took over 8 s - an unbounded loop, a regex, an unindexed search; one request should not tie the app up

slow-door.label: door over budget
slow-door.why: one request alone took longer than the budget (## Tests budget:, default 1000 ms) - a missing index, an N+1, a call out

door-folds-under-load.label: door folds under ten
door-folds-under-load.why: fine alone, but ten requests at once push its p95 past three budgets - this is what launch day looks like

door-regressed.label: door slower than last run
door-regressed.why: more than twice as slow as the previous test run - something in the last change costs time

format-drift.label: formatting drift
format-drift.why: two indent styles, two line endings, trailing blanks or no final newline in one file - the sign of several hands (or models) and no formatter; run one

format-prettier.label: not formatted (prettier)
format-prettier.why: the project has prettier and a config, and this file does not match it

file-without-kind.label: no kind of its own
file-without-kind.why: a code file in a feature that is not a screen, an action, logic or data by shape, with no @kind - the shape rules cannot judge what they cannot place

login-failed.label: test sign-in failed
login-failed.why: the login door under ## Tests did not sign the test user in - the seed lacks the user, or the door changed; every door behind the login went unprobed

door-refuses-user.label: door refuses the test user
door-refuses-user.why: refused signed in as well as signed out - fine for an admin door, a break for one a plain user should reach; the role matrix decides which

restore-failed.label: restore drill failed
restore-failed.why: backup then restore on the test database did not come back equal - the backup that would save prod does not work

restore-unproven.label: restore never drilled
restore-unproven.why: no backup/restore scripts (or ## Backup commands) - a backup nobody has restored from is a hope, not a backup

backup-stale.label: backups stopped
backup-stale.why: the newest file in the declared backup folder is older than the schedule allows - the nightly job is not running

backup-none.label: no backup has landed
backup-none.why: the declared backup folder is empty

backup-folder-missing.label: backup folder unreadable
backup-folder-missing.why: the folder under ## Backup cannot be read from the engine's machine

backup-undeclared.label: backup folder not declared
backup-undeclared.why: no folder: under ## Backup - the scan cannot tell whether backups are landing

architecture-doc-handwritten.label: ARCHITECTURE.md hand-written
architecture-doc-handwritten.why: the schema lives in tags.json and this file is generated from it; a hand-written one drifts from the schema without anyone noticing

doctrine-review-due.label: doctrine review due
doctrine-review-due.why: five lessons wait in the inbox, or the oldest is over a month old - a lesson unpromoted is a lesson unlearned

risk._note: the matrix: likelihood (1-5: the check weight, +1 if the file changed 3+ times in 90 days, +1 if untested, -1 if unchanged in 90 days) x impact (1-5, the impact lens). Bands by the product.
